source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Shakuntala sub-parva, and the opening of the Yayati tale. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.69.28–51, 1.70.28–46 and 1.71.1–9 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): as Shakuntala set out, a bodiless voice from the sky spoke to Duhshanta, who sat among his sacrificial priests, house priest, teachers and ministers (1.69.28); support your son, Duhshanta; do not scorn Shakuntala (1.69.29: the hook, bharasva putram); you are the begetter of this child; Shakuntala has spoken the truth (1.69.30: `voice`); because he is to be supported (bhartavya) by you at our word, let your son be Bharata by name (1.69.33: `name`); hearing the speech of the heaven-dwellers the Paurava king, overjoyed, said to his priest and ministers (1.69.34: `glad`): hear, sirs, what this messenger of the gods says; I too know him to be my own son (1.69.35: `knew`, the turn); if I had taken him as my son on her word alone, the people would have doubted and he would not be cleared (1.69.36: `why`); he received his son with joy, smelled (kissed) his head and embraced him with love (1.69.37–38: `embrace`); he honoured his wife according to law and said, soothing her: our union was made out of the world's sight, so I did this to clear you (1.69.39–41); and what you said to me in anger, beloved, I forgive (1.69.42: `queen`: in the CE it is he who forgives; no apology of his is recorded, and the line says only what the text says); he named his son Bharata and consecrated him young king (1.69.44); his famed wheel rolled on, bright, divine, unconquered; he conquered the kings of the earth, was a wheel-turning universal king (1.69.45–47: `wheel`); Kanva was his priest in great sacrifices (1.69.48; not used); from Bharata comes the Bharata fame, and through him this family is Bharata, and those before and after are called Bharatas (1.69.49: `line`, the lit payoff); Yayati, son of Nahusha, had sons by Devayani and Sharmishtha, among them Puru, whose line the Pauravas are (1.70.29–32, 45); Janamejaya: how did our forefather Yayati win the daughter of Shukra, so hard to win (1.71.1: the cliffhanger); Shukra raised the slain danavas by his knowledge (1.71.7). NOT IN THE CE and not said: that the land of Bharata (India) is named for this Bharata (1.69.49 speaks of the family and its fame). CE AGAINST THE CATALOG PLAN: the plan's cliffhanger said Yayati "paid a terrible price for desire"; that is his own tale (1.70.33–46, 1.78–80), many episodes on; the handover is now the king's actual next question (1.71.1), which the next episode answers.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

lines.speaker: skyvoice
lines.note: COLD OPEN (direct speech from above; no fire): looking straight up from the floor of a hall: pillars converge on an opening full of bright cloud; light pours down; small faces at the rim all turned up. The card low.

lines.text: Before his whole court, King Dushyanta had denied Shakuntala and their son.
lines.say: Before his whole court, [p:100] King Dushyanta [p:60] had denied Shakuntala [p:60] and their son.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): the red-and-gold hall: the king on his feet at the throne (plaque: Dushyanta · the king who denied his wife), and at the doors, about to leave, the woman in bark cloth with her boy (plaque: Shakuntala · his wife, raised in a hermitage). A track from him to her.

lines.speaker: skyvoice
lines.text: "Shakuntala has spoken the truth. Do not scorn her."
lines.say: Shakuntala has spoken the truth. [p:350] Do not scorn her.
lines.note: STORY 1 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (sun-white; answers the hook and episode 57's question): a crane up from the two at the doors: a column of white light comes down through the roof onto mother and son; everyone else in the hall falls into blue shadow; courtiers shield their eyes. The voice has no body: only the light (sub: a bodiless voice · Adi 1.69.28–30).

lines.speaker: skyvoice
lines.text: "You must support him: so let his name be Bharata."
lines.say: You must support him: [p:300] so let his name [p:60] be Bharata.
lines.note: STORY 2 (messenger-dawn): the boy alone in the light, looking up, unafraid, a hand shading his eyes (plaque: BHARATA · "the one to be supported"; sub: bhara · support).

lines.text: The king turned, overjoyed, to his priests and ministers.
lines.say: The king turned, [p:80] overjoyed, [p:100] to his priests and ministers.
lines.note: STORY 3 (wedding-turmeric: the hall warm again): the king swings round to the rows of priests and ministers, both arms opening, his whole face alight; they stare at him.

lines.speaker: dushyanta
lines.text: "Hear the messenger of the gods! I too knew he was my son."
lines.say: Hear the messenger of the gods! [p:350] I too knew [p:80] he was my son.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %) after a real silence · THE CLOSE-UP (war-iron: the dark of the hall behind him): the king's face fills the frame: triumph, then the mask comes off: relief and shame together (the brows lift and knit, the eyes go down to the boy). The word of the turn: KNEW.

lines.speaker: dushyanta
lines.text: "On her word alone, the people would have doubted him."
lines.say: On her word alone, [p:200] the people would have doubted him.
lines.note: STORY 5: a rack focus from the king's open hand in the foreground to the ranks of courtiers behind, whispering, one pointing: the people he feared (sub: Adi 1.69.36).

lines.text: He kissed the boy's head and held him close.
lines.say: He kissed the boy's head [p:120] and held him close.
lines.note: STORY 6 (island-gold): the king comes down the throne steps, kneels and gathers the boy in both arms, his crowned head bent over the child's (a father and a small child: the one embrace in the arc; drawn as carry-and-kneel, the boy's face clear over his shoulder).

lines.text: He honoured her as his queen, and forgave her angry words.
lines.say: He honoured her as his queen, [p:200] and forgave [p:60] her angry words.
lines.note: STORY 7 (brahma-rose): Shakuntala, now in a queen's rose sari and jewels, seated beside the throne, the king's hands joined toward her; her face composed, not smiling, her eyes on her son (tag: "I forgive what you said in anger" · the king, Adi 1.69.42).

lines.text: Bharata became a king of kings. No one could stop his chariot wheel.
lines.say: Bharata became a king of kings. [p:300] No one could stop [p:60] his chariot wheel.
lines.note: STORY 8 · NEW LIGHT (hunt-emerald): Bharata grown: a broad young king in a war chariot crossing a green land at full speed, a great bright wheel turning ahead of him over hills and rivers; small kings bow at the roadside.

lines.text: From him, this whole line is called the Bharatas.
lines.say: From him, [p:150] this whole line [p:80] is called the Bharatas.
lines.note: THE LIT PAYOFF (a second real silence before it; ≥ 4 s with its hold; release-gold): a tilt up a painted family tree in gold light: Bharata at its root, crowned, Shakuntala beside him; above, branch on branch of small kings rising out of frame (plaque: THE BHARATAS · his line: the family of this story; sub: Adi 1.69.49).

lines.text: The end of an arc · Shakuntala
lines.note: The ARC-END CARD (silent): over the gold tree, a lacquer cartouche with a flame border: THE END OF AN ARC · SHAKUNTALA · Episodes 53–58 · the playlist line.

lines.text: Long before Bharata, his forefather Yayati married the daughter of a sage who could raise the dead.
lines.say: Long before Bharata, [p:100] his forefather Yayati [p:80] married the daughter of a sage [p:200] who could raise the dead.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the king's own next question, CE 1.71.1): a tilt down the same tree to an older root: a crowned king (plaque: Yayati · a forefather of the line) and beside him a proud young woman; behind her, vast and dim in violet, a gaunt sage with a raised hand, and at his feet a fallen warrior sitting up. The source line (top).
